description: Map deskfile database for the welfare profile: Work and Income's public reference tables (rates current and historical, area codes, thresholds, calendars) from workandincome.govt.nz/map/deskfile. Crown copyright, licensed for re-use under CC BY 4.0: attribute the Ministry of Social Development (and indicate changes - the tables have been extracted and reformatted for retrieval). Point-in-time research snapshot, not the official or current tables. Kept separate from the semantic policy corpus because the tables are exact lookups, not policy text. Each document has a title, section path, keyword tokens and a markdown rendering of its tables; the agent searches by keyword with search_deskfile and reads the exact table with read_deskfile.

documents.title: Approved business enterprises
documents.section: approved business enterprises
documents.text:
## Approved business enterprises

Approved business enterprises are community-based organisations that provide vocational services for people with disabilities (these enterprises were previously known as sheltered workshops). Clients employed in an approved business enterprise are considered to be working in sheltered employment for Supported Living Payment purposes.

Below is a list of these, sorted using MSD regions.

documents.text:
## At 15 February 2021

Below are the maximum Flexi-wage Subsidy rates at 15 February 2021. Flexi-wage has 3 different pay bands.

## Payment bands and payment amount

| Band | Payment amount (including GST) |
| --- | --- |
| Band 1 | $276 gross per week for 24 consecutive weeks ($6,624 in total, gross) |
| Band 2 | $276 gross per week for 36 consecutive weeks ($9,936 in total, gross) |
| Band 3 | A discretionary rate, depending on the person's circumstances. The maximum payable is equivalent to the adult minimum wage for 30 hours work per week, up to $22,000 (gross) in a 52-week period. |

Note when Flexi-Wage is granted for a person working less than 30 hours per week, a pro-rata subsidy is paid.

documents.title: At 5 August 2020
documents.section: employment and training information > mana in mahi tables
documents.text:
## At 5 August 2020

Below are the maximum Mana in Mahi rates at 5 August 2020. The actual rates depend on the client's individual circumstances.

| Category | Maximum amount |
| --- | --- |
| Wage subsidy | Up to $16,000 (plus GST) for the participant's first year in Mana in Mahi, and up to $8,000 (plus GST) for the second year (this rate is paid proportionally for part-time employment) |
| Support with training (pre-employment or on-the-job) | Up to $2,000 (plus GST) as agreed at the start of the Mana in Mahi contract |
| Fees for education or training course | Up to $16,000 in total (plus GST) over 2 years (and not more than $8,000 within a 52-week period) towards course fees (where fees are not already covered by other fees-free initiatives such as Fees Free or Targeted Training and Apprenticeship Fund) |
| Incentive payments | Up to $6,000 in total over 2 years (and not more than $3,000 within a 52-week period) at attendance and training milestones |
| Additional educational support costs | Up to $4,000 in total over 2 years (and not more than $2,000 within a 52-week period) for the actual and reasonable costs of any additional educational support costs |

## Current rates

For the current rates see:

- Mana in Mahi rates (current)

## Mana in Mahi rates (current)

Below are the maximum Mana in Mahi rates at 5 August 2022. The actual rates depend on the client's individual circumstances.

| Category | Maximum amount |
| --- | --- |
| Wage subsidy | Up to $16,000 (plus GST) over 1 year (this is paid proportionally for part-time employment) |
| Support with training (pre-employment or on-the-job) | Up to $2,000 (plus GST) as agreed at the start of the Mana in Mahi contract |
| Fees for education or training course | Up to $8,000 (plus GST) over 1 year towards training course fees (where fees are not covered by other publicly funded assistance) |
| Incentive payments | Up to $3,000 over 1 year (paid in instalments of $1,000) at attendance and training milestones |
| Additional educational support costs | Up to $2,000 over 1 year for the actual and reasonable costs of any additional educational support costs |

Below are the four areas used for the calculation of Accommodation Supplement from 1 April 2018. The locations within each area are sorted alphabetically.

The locations listed below relate specifically to the names of the Statistical Area Units 2017, as defined by Statistics New Zealand. They are not equivalent to postal address suburbs, towns or cities, despite occasionally sharing similar names.

To confirm an area code for a specific address, use CMS or the Accommodation Supplement area map [no link find out why] tool.

## Entry thresholds and maximum rates

For the entry thresholds and maximum rates of Accommodation Supplement see:

- Jobseeker Support

- Jobseeker Support Student Hardship

- New Zealand Superannuation and Veterans Pension

- Sole Parent Support

- Supported Living Payment

- Young Parent Payment

- Youth Payment

- Non-beneficiaries

- Couples on different benefits

- Clients with partners in care

For an Emergency Benefit or Emergency Maintenance Allowance client, the entry thresholds and maximum rates are the same as those for the equivalent benefit (the benefit that the client is paid).

## Temporary Additional Support

For the maximum rates of Accommodation Supplement for determining the upper limit for certain refugees, protected persons or residence applicants for Temporary Additional Support see:

## Historical rates

Historical rates are amounts related to assistance that is no longer available. For these rates, see:

- Accommodation Supplement thresholds and maximum rates last updated on 1 April 2013

## At 1 October 2010

Below are the standard Foster Care allowance rates at 1 October 2010. These are non-taxable, weekly rates.

| Category | Non-taxable rate | Temporary GST Assistance - see Note 1 below |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Child 0 - 4 years | $134.91 | $2.73 |
| Child 5 - 9 years | $156.56 | $3.16 |
| Child 10 - 13 years | $172.77 | $3.49 |
| Child 14+ years | $188.88 | $3.82 |
| Family home | $176.13 | $3.56 |

## Note 1

Temporary GST Assistance is:

- a payment intended to compensate clients for the GST (goods and services tax) increase from 12.5% to 15% on 1 October 2010

- payable from 1 October 2010 to 31 March 2011 (from 1 April 2011, it's expected that benefit rates increased by the annual general adjustment will incorporate cost-of-living increases since 1 October 2010)

- equal to 2.02% of the non-taxable weekly benefit rate, and is always paid in full

- paid automatically, at the same time as the main benefit payment

- not taxable or classed as income

documents.section: extra help information > funeral grant tables
documents.text:
## Income limits (current)

## Deceased person with a surviving partner

A Funeral Grant can be paid for a deceased person with a surviving partner, if the surviving partner's income is below the following limit - at 1 April 2026:

| Category | Gross annual income limit |
| --- | --- |
| Surviving partner, 16 - 17 years (without children) | $33,518.68 |
| Surviving partner, 18+ years (without children) | $38,522.12 |
| Surviving partner with 1 child | $46,745.92 |
| Surviving partner with 2+ children | $49,248.68 |

The income test does not apply to a Funeral Grant for a deceased single person (whether or not there is a surviving child).

## Deceased child

A Funeral Grant can be paid for a child, if the parental income is below the following limit - at 1 April 2026:

| Category | Gross annual income limit |
| --- | --- |
| Parent is single, 16 - 17 years (with no other children) | $33,518.68 |
| Parent is single, 18+ years (with no other children) | $38,522.12 |
| Parent is in a marriage, civil union or de facto relationship (with or without other children) | $55,954.08 |
| Parent is single with 1 other child | $46,745.92 |
| Parent is single with 2+ other children | $49,248.68 |

| $1,047.43 - $1,117.42 | 5 weeks | $1,257.43 - and over | 10 weeks |  |

## More than 5 children

The initial stand-down period charts provided have only been assessed for a married couple or sole parent with up to 5 dependent children. When a client has more than 5 dependent children to be taken into account, you will need to adjust the average income range in the assessment charts.

You need to select the particular family circumstance plus 5 children and add $50 per week onto the average income range for each additional dependent child to be taken into account.

Example

To find the initial stand-down period for a married couple with 7 dependent children who have an average income of $1,017.41 per week.

Step 1. Select the initial stand-down assessment for a married couple with 5 dependent children as at 9 May 2001:

| Average income | Initial stand-down |
| --- | --- |
| $000.00 - $917.42 | 1 week |
| $917.43 - $987.42 | 2 weeks |
| $987.43 - $1,057.42 | 3 weeks |
| $1,057.43 - $1,127.42 | 4 weeks |
| $1,127.43 - $1,197.42 | 5 weeks |

Step 2. Adjust this assessment by $100 per week (that is 2 X $50) to reflect a married couple with 7 dependent children.

| Average income | Initial stand-down |
| --- | --- |
| $000.00 - $1,017.42 | 1 week |
| $1,017.43 - $1,087.42 | 2 weeks |
| $1,087.43 - $1,157.42 | 3 weeks |
| $1,157.43 - $1,227.42 | 4 weeks |
| $1,227.43 - $1,297.42 | 5 weeks |

Result. The initial stand-down period for a married couple with 7 dependent children and an average income of $1,017.41 per week would be 1 week.

documents.title: Formula for initial stand-down periods
documents.section: initial stand down
documents.text:
## Formula for initial stand-down periods

The following information is about the formula used to calculate initial stand-down periods. For the current and previous stand-down periods see:

- Introduction

Initial stand-down periods are calculated using the gross Average Ordinary Time Weekly Wage (AOTWW) rate, which is determined every 3 months by Statistics New Zealand using their Quarterly Employment Survey.

## Unadjusted formula

The unadjusted formula is for a married, civil union or de facto couple with no dependent children. The unadjusted formula is as follows:

| Initial stand-down period | Unadjusted formula (married, civil union or de facto couple) |
| --- | --- |
| 1 week | Less than the AOTWW |
| 2 weeks | AOTWW and over |

The maximum initial stand-down period reduced from 10 weeks to 2 weeks, on 2 July 2007.

## Formula adjustment

To take into account a client's family circumstances this formula is adjusted as follows:

- $80 per week is added to the allowable average income for each dependent child (this increased from $50 on 1 April 2005) and

- $80 per week is deducted from the allowable average income for single or sole parents

## Average weekly income

Clients can choose an income assessment period of either 26 or 52 weeks to calculate their gross average weekly income for stand-down purposes. You will need to calculate the gross average weekly income for both a 26 and 52 week period.

To calculate the average weekly income over a 26 week period, divide by 26, the total amount of income received by the client in the 26 week period immediately before their entitlement date.

To calculate the average weekly income over a 52 week period, divide by 52, the total amount of income received by the client in the 52 week period immediately before their entitlement date.

You should use the calculation that gives the client a lesser stand-down period.

For more information on average weekly income refer to the commencement date section of each main benefit.

## For the current rates see:

- Current stand-down periods

## Note 1

Temporary GST Assistance is:

- a payment intended to compensate clients for the GST (goods and services tax) increase from 12.5% to 15% on 1 October 2010

- payable from 1 October 2010 to 31 March 2011 (from 1 April 2011, it's expected that benefit rates increased by the annual general adjustment will incorporate cost-of-living increases since 1 October 2010)

- equal to 2.02% of the non-taxable weekly benefit rate, and is always paid in full

- paid automatically, at the same time as the main benefit payment

- not taxable or classed as income

documents.title: Emergency Benefit
documents.section: main benefits rates
documents.text:
## Emergency Benefit

The Emergency Benefit rate is usually the appropriate Jobseeker Support rate, unless the client is:

- caring for a person or

- on residential parole in a habilitation programme or

- permanently restricted for work or

- non residentially qualified for Supported Living Payment

- not lawfully resident or present for youth support payments

documents.section: main benefits rates
documents.text:
## Emergency Maintenance Allowance

For an Emergency Maintenance Allowance client, the rates are the same as those for the equivalent benefit (the benefit that the client is paid).

documents.title: Accommodation Benefit rates prior to 2001
documents.section: student support tables > accommodation benefit rates
documents.text:
## Accommodation Benefit rates prior to 2001

The delivery of Student Allowances was transferred from the Ministry of Education to the then Department of Work and Income from 1 January 1999. This included the methodology for calculating the Accommodation Benefit rates.

The current methodology and approach has largely been in place since the commencement of the scheme, under the Student Allowances Regulations 1991, from 1 January 1992.

Up until 1999 there was no need for what is now called the "rural rate". In May 1999 it was noted that a number of newly recognised institutions had been set up in small rural locations for which there were no rates. This resulted in a decision to calculate the mean rate for all rural areas and provide a generic "rural rate" for those small rural locations, as well as for other areas where there is insufficient bond data to establish a separate rate.

The rates for the 2000 calendar year were not updated from the 1999 rates as a strict application of the proposed news rates would have resulted in a reduction for many rates. It was not considered appropriate to reduce Accommodation Benefit rates when in the benefit system rates do not reduce.

From the 2001 calendar year and onwards, a decision was made to only change Accommodation Benefit rates where there is an increase in the rate.

For more information see:

- Accommodation Benefit

documents.text:
## Overseas study - regions and specified countries

For study starting on or after 1 January 2017, students studying at an overseas campus or delivery site of a New Zealand tertiary provider must be studying in a specified country, as listed below.

This requirement applies to both Student Allowances and Student Loans.

For Student Allowance purposes, the list of specified countries are set out in Schedule 3A, Student Allowances Regulations 1998.

| Region | Country |
| --- | --- |
| Asia | Brunei Darussalam Cambodia China Hong Kong India Indonesia Japan Laos Malaysia Myanmar Philippines Republic of Korea Singapore Sri Lanka Taiwan Thailand Viet Nam |
| Latin America | Argentina Brazil Chile Colombia Mexico Paraguay Peru Uruguay |
| Middle East | Iran Oman Saudi Arabia United Arab Emirates |

## For more information see:

- Student Allowances Study overseas

- Student Loans Study overseas

## Legislation

- Regions and countries Schedule 3A Student Allowances Regulations 1998

## At 1 April 2016

## Introduction

Student Allowance rates are aligned with Jobseeker Support rates. The rates take into account such things as the age of the student and whether they live with their parents.

Rates for students 24 years or over are not subject to the parental income test.

From 1 January 2009 the age threshold for the parental income test was reduced from 25 to 24.

From 1 April 2016, students with a supported child or children will receive an increase to their Student Allowance rate of $25.00 per week, as a result of the Child in Material Hardship package announced as part of Budget 2015:

- A single student with a supported child or children will receive an increase of $25.00 per week

- Where both parents are students and they are in a recognised relationship, and they are both receiving a Student Allowance, they will each receive an increase of $12.50 per week

- Where both parents are students and in a recognised relationship, (but where one student does not receive or is not eligible for an allowance), the other student will receive an increase of $25.00 per week

- Where both parents are students and they both receive a Student Allowance, but are separated and they have a shared custody arrangement for their children, they will each receive an increase of $25.00 per week

- Where one parent is a student and in receipt of a Student Allowance, and the other parent is a beneficiary, and they have a shared custody arrangement for their children, they will each receive $25.00 per week

- Where one parent is a student in receipt of a Student Allowance, and the other parent is not a student or a beneficiary, and they have a shared custody arrangement for their children, the student will receive an increase of $25.00 per week

The rates where the combined income is not more than $423.92 (as at 1 April 2015) and between $423.92 and $882.98 (as at 1 April 2015), were previously referred to as "dependent" and "earning" partner rates (respectively). These terms are no longer used as a result of the new rates introduced from 1 April 2016, and because they are no longer useful terms.

Set out below are Student Allowance weekly rates at 1 April 2016 together with a description of the equivalent Jobseeker Support rate.

Only rates with a supported child changed as there was no adjustment to the other rates because the calculated CPI movement produced a negative figure.

For more information about the CPI adjustment as part of the Annual General Adjustment (AGA), see:

## Students with a partner in a recognised relationship

For Student Allowance purposes, a recognised relationship is where the student and their partner are both 24 or over, or one or both of them are under 24 and they have a supported child or children. If a relationship is not recognised, the student is treated as being "single" for the purposes of assessing entitlement.

The following couple rates of Student Allowance apply to students in a recognised relationship.

Couple combined weekly income of not more than $423.92 – without supported children

| Rate description | Net amount after "M" tax rate | Gross amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The student's spouse or partner is not enrolled in more than half of a full-time course, and the student is childless | $350.20 | $401.64 |

This (net) rate after "M" tax is deducted is equivalent to the Jobseeker Support rate for a married, civil union or de facto couple, without children. The gross rate is higher than the Jobseeker Support rate for a married, civil union or de facto couple, without children due to the fact that in the benefit system the payment is apportioned between both partners. Therefore the applicable tax calculation is for two "married" individuals. For Student Allowances only one partner receives the payment and is taxed at the single rate. This results in a greater overall amount of tax being calculated for the Student allowance recipient.

| Rate description | Net amount after "M" tax rate | Gross amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The student's spouse or partner is enrolled in more than half of a full-time course but does not receive, and is not eligible for, a grant, and the student is childless | $210.13 | $234.78 |

This rate is equivalent to the Jobseeker Support rate for a single person 25 years of age or over.

## At 1 April 2022 - Parental income abatement calculation - living at home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living at home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold.

When the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold, the gross Student Allowance payable is reduced as follows:

| Gross parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.2793296% (at 1 April 2022) | = B (amount by which the gross rate of Student Allowance will be reduced) |
| Gross Student Allowance rate minus B | = C (Gross Student Allowance payable after abatement, if any) |

documents.section: student support tables > student allowance rates and thresholds
documents.text:
## At 1 April 2022 - Parental income abatement calculation - living away from home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living away from home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income is over the parental income threshold.

There are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount by which the parental income exceeds the parental income threshold. Use either Calculation 1 or 2 (not both).

Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by up to $8,113.04 (or $156.02 a week)

When the gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $8,113.04, reduce the gross Student Allowance payable as follows:

| Gross parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.30303% (at 1 April 2022) | = B (amount by which the gross rate of Student Allowance will be reduced) |
| Gross Student Allowance rate minus B | = C (Gross Student Allowance payable after abatement, if any) |

Or

Calculation 2: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by more than $8,113.04 (or $156.02 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $8,113.04, reduce the gross Student Allowance payable by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $8,113.04 by 0.30303% = $2,458.49. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by $2,458.49 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the threshold (in excess of $8,113.04) by 0.2793296%. Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

| Calculation 2 example: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000 |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Calculation using gross annual figures using | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2022) | $60,968.96 | $1,172.48 gross a week |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $104,000 - $60,968.96 = $43,031.04 | $2,000 - $1,172.48 = $827.52 |
| Calculation 2 | Step 1: 0.30303 x $8,113.04 = $2,458.49 (rounded) Step 2: $43,031.04 - $8,113.04 = $34,918.00 0.2793296 x $34,918.00 = $9,753.63 (rounded) | Step 1: 0.30303 x $156.02 = $47.28 (rounded) Step 2: $827.52 - $156.02 = $671.50 0.2793296 x $671.50 = $187.57 (rounded) |
| Gross Student Allowance payable (from 1 April 2022) | $16,458.52 Less $2,458.50 (Step 1) Less $9,753.63 (Step 2) = $4,246.39 Gross annual Student Allowance payable (after abatement) | $316.51 Less $47.28 (Step 1) Less $187.57 (Step 2) = $81.66 Gross weekly Student Allowance payable (after abatement) |

## At 1 April 2023 - Parental income abatement calculation - living away from home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living away from home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income is over the parental income threshold.

From 1 April 2022, there are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount the parental income exceeds the parental income threshold. These abatement calculations now change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either Calculation 1 or 2 (not both).

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by up to $12,317.24 (or $236.87 a week)

When the gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $12,317.24, reduce the gross Student Allowance payable as follows:

| Gross parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 1 April 2023) | = B (amount by which the gross rate of Student Allowance will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance (gross) rate minus B | = C (Student Allowance (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Calculation 2: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by more than $12,317.24 (or $236.87 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $12,317.24 (or $236.87 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payable by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $12,317.24 (or $236.87 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $3,732.49. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by $3,732.49 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the threshold (in excess of $12,317.24) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000.00

| Calculation 2 example: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000 |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2023) | $65,370.76 | $1,257.13 gross a week |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $104,000 - $65,370.76 = $38,629.24 | $2,000 - $1,257.13 = $742.87 |
| Calculation 2 | Step 1: $12,317.24 x 0.3030303 = $3,732.49 | Step 1: $236.87 x 0.3030303 = $71.77 |
|  | Step 2: $38,629.24 - $12,317.24 = $26,312.00 | Step 2: $742.87 - $236.87 = $506.00 |
|  | $26,312.00 x 0.2793296 = $7,349.72 | $506.00 x 0.2793296 = $141.34 |
| Student Allowance (gross) payable (from 1 April 2023) | $17,732.52 Less $3,732.49 (Step 1) Less $7,349.72 (Step 2) = $6,650.31 annual (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) | $341.01 Less $71.77 (Step 1) Less $141.34 (Step 2) = $127.90 weekly (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) |

| Parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 1 April 2023) | = B (amount the gross Student Allowance rate will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance rate (gross) minus B | = C (Student Allowance rate (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Or

## Calculation 2: Annual parental income (gross) exceeds the parental income threshold by more than $3,445.52 (or $66.26 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $3,445.52 (or $66.26 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payment by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $3,445.52 (or $66.26 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $1,044.09. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate by $1,044.09 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold (in excess of $3,445.52) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have annual parental income of $90,507.43 (gross)

|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2023) | $65,370.76 | $1,257.13 |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $90,507.43 - $65,370.76 = $25,136.67 | $1,740.52 - $1,257.13 = $483.39 |
| Calculation | Step 1: $3,445.52 x 0.3030303 = $1,044.09 | Step 1: $66.26 x 0.3030303 = $20.07 |
| Step 2: $25,136.67 - $3,445.52 = $21,691.15 | Step 2: $483.39 - $66.26 = $417.13 |  |
| $21,691.15 x 0.2793296 = $6,058.98 | $417.13 x 0.2793296 = $116.51 |  |
| Student Allowance (gross) payment (from 1 April 2023) | $15,044.12 Less $1,044.09 (step 1) Less $6,058.98 (step 2) | $289.31 Less $20.07 (step 1) Less $116.51 (step 2) |
| = $7,941.05 annual Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) | = $152.73 weekly Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) |  |

## At 1 April 2025 - Parental income abatement calculation - living away from home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living away from home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income is over the parental income threshold.

From 1 April 2022, there are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount the parental income exceeds the parental income threshold. These abatement calculations now change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either Calculation 1 or 2 (not both).

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by up to $11,404.64 (or $219.32 a week)

When the gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $11,404.64, reduce the gross Student Allowance payable as follows:

| Gross parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 1 April 2025) | = B (amount by which the gross rate of Student Allowance will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance (gross) rate minus B | = C (Student Allowance (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Calculation 2: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by more than $11,404.64 (or $219.32 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $11,404.64 (or $219.32 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payable by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $11,404.64 (or $219.32 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $3,455.95. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by $3,455.95 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the threshold (in excess of $11,404.64) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000.00

|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2025) | $69,935.32 | $1,344.91 |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $104,000 - $69,935.32 = $34,064.68 | $2,000 - $1,344.91 = $655.09 |
| Calculation 2 | Step 1: $11,404.64 x 0.3030303 = $3,455.95 | Step 1: $219.32 x 0.3030303 = $66.46 |
|  | Step 2: $34,064.68 - $11,404.64 = $22,660.04 | Step 2: $655.09 - $219.32 = $435.77 |
|  | $22,660.04 x 0.2793296 = $6,329.61 | $435.77 x 0.2793296 = $121.72 |
| Student Allowance (gross) payable (from 1 April 2025) | $19,055.92 Less $3,455.95 (step 1) Less $6,329.61 (step 2) = $9,270.34 annual (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) | $366.46 Less $66.46 (step 1) Less $121.72 (step 2) = $178.27 weekly (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) |

Note Figures are not rounded or truncated during calculation, but the final Student Allowance payable is truncated to 2 decimal places.

## At 1 April 2025 - Parental income abatement calculation - living at home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living at home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold.

There are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount by which the parental income exceeds the annual parental income threshold. These abatement calculations will change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either calculation 1 or 2 (not both). The calculations used below are as at 1 April 2025.

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by up to $1,918.28 (or $36.89 a week)

When the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $1,918.28, the Student Allowance (gross) payable is reduced as follows:

| Parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 1 April 2025) | = B (amount the gross Student Allowance rate will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance rate (gross) minus B | = C (Student Allowance rate (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Calculation 2: Annual parental income (gross) exceeds the parental income threshold by more than $1,918.28 (or $36.89 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $1,918.28 (or $36.89 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payment by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $1,918.28 (or $36.89 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $581.29. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate by $581.29, and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold (in excess of $1,918.28) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have annual parental income of $90,507.43 (gross)

|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2025) | $69,935.32 | $1,344.91 |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $90,507.43 - $69,935.32 = $20,572.11 | $1,740.52 - $1,344.91 = $395.61 |
| Calculation | Step 1: $1,918.28 x 0.3030303 = $581.29 | Step 1: $36.89 x 0.3030303 = $11.17 |
| Step 2: $20,572.11 - $1,918.28 = $18,653.83 | Step 2: $395.61 - $36.89 = $358.72 |  |
| $18,653.83 x 0.2793296 = $5,210.56 | $358.72 x 0.2793296 = $100.20 |  |
| Student Allowance (gross) payment (from 1 April 2025) | $16,181.36 Less $581.29 (step 1) Less $5,210.56 (step 2) | $311.19 Less $11.17 (step 1) Less $100.20 (step 2) |
| = $10,390.01 annual Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) | = $199.80 weekly Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) |  |

## At 1 January 2018

## Introduction

Student Allowance rates take into account things such as the age of the student and whether they live with their parents.

They have historically been aligned with Jobseeker Support rates. A one-off increase of $50 (and $100 for particular couple rates) to the net Student Allowance rates (with a tax code of M) from 1 January 2018 changed this historical alignment.

Rates for "single" students under 24 years of age are subject to the parental-income test.

documents.text:
## At 31 July 2024 - Parental income abatement calculation - living away from home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living away from home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income is over the parental income threshold.

From 1 April 2022, there are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount the parental income exceeds the parental income threshold. These abatement calculations now change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either Calculation 1 or 2 (not both).

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by up to $9,942.40 (or $191.20 a week)

When the gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $9,942.40, reduce the gross Student Allowance payable as follows:

| Gross parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 31 July 2024) | = B (amount by which the gross rate of Student Allowance will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance (gross) rate minus B | = C (Student Allowance (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Calculation 2: Gross annual parental income exceeds the threshold by more than $9,942.40 (or $191.20 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $9,942.40 (or $191.20 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payable by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $9,942.40 (or $191.20 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $3,012.84. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by $3,012.84 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the threshold (in excess of $9,942.40) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000.00

| Calculation 2 example: A student's parents have gross annual parental income of $104,000 |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| Parental income threshold (from 31 July 2024) | $68,413.80 | $1,315.65 gross a week |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $104,000 - $68,413.80 = $35,586.20 | $2,000 - $1,315.65 = $684.35 |
| Calculation 2 | Step 1: $9,942.40 x 0.3030303 Abatement 1 = $3,012.84 | Step 1: $191.20 x 0.3030303 Abatement 1 = $57.93 |
|  | Step 2: $35,586.20 - $9,942.40 = $25,643.80 | Step 2: $684.35 - $191.20 = $493.15 |
|  | $25,643.80 x 0.2793296 Abatement 2 = $7,163.07 | $493.15 x 0.2793296 Abatement 2 = $137.75 |
| Student Allowance (gross) payable (from 31 July 2024) | $18,612.88 Less abatement 1 Less abatement 2 = $8,436.95 annual (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) | $357.94 Less abatement 1 Less abatement 2 = $162.24 weekly (gross) Student Allowance payable (after abatement) |

## At 31 July 2024 - Parental income abatement calculation - living at home rate

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living at home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold.

There are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount by which the parental income exceeds the annual parental income threshold. These abatement calculations will change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either calculation 1 or 2 (not both). The calculations used below are as at 31 July 2024.

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by up to $660.92 (or $12.71 a week)

When the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $660.92 (or $12.71 a week), the Student Allowance (gross) payable is reduced as follows:

| Parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 31 July 2024) | = B (amount the gross Student Allowance rate will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance rate (gross) minus B | = C (Student Allowance rate (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Or

## Calculation 2: Annual parental income (gross) exceeds the parental income threshold by more than $660.92 (or $12.71 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $660.92 (or $12.71 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payment by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $660.92 (or $12.71 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $200.27. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate by $200.27, and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold (in excess of $660.92) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in Step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have annual parental income of $90,480 (gross)

|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parental income threshold (from 31 July 2024) | $68,413.80 | $1,315.65 |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $90,480 - $68,413.80 = $22,066.20 | $1,740 - $1,315.65 = $424.35 |
| Calculation | Step 1: $660.92 x 0.3030303 Abatement 1 = $200.27 | Step 1: $12.71 x 0.3030303 Abatement 1 = $3.85 |
| Step 2: $22,066.20 - $660.92 = $21,405.28 | Step 2: $424.35 - $12.71 = $411.64 |  |
| $21,405.28 x 0.2793296 Abatement 2 = $5,979.12 | $411.64 x 0.2793296 = $114.98 |  |
| Student Allowance (gross) payment (from 31 July 2024) | $15,800.20 Less abatement 1 Less abatement 2 | $303.85 Less abatement 1 Less abatement 2 |
| = $9620.79 annual Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) | = $185.01 weekly Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) |  |

## Combined income limits (current)

Below is the Student Allowance combined (couple) income threshold and cut out point at 1 April 2026. These are gross, weekly limits.

| Threshold | Cut-out point |

| $569.40 | $1,185.75 |

A higher rate of Student Allowance will be paid if a couple's combined income is $569.40 gross or less per week.

If a couple's combined income is more than $569.40 gross per week but less than $1,185.75 gross per week then Student Allowance will be paid at a lower rate.

In any week that a couple's combined income is $1,185.75 gross or more there will be no entitlement to Student Allowance.

## Parental income abatement calculation - living at home rate (current)

The gross rate of Student Allowance payable for students under 24, single, childless and living at home is abated (reduced) if the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold.

There are two separate abatement calculations, depending on the amount by which the parental income exceeds the annual parental income threshold. These abatement calculations will change every year as part of annual general adjustments.

Use either calculation 1 or 2 (not both). The calculations used below are as at 1 April 2026.

## Calculation 1: Gross annual parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by up to $3,713.32 (or $71.41 a week)

When the gross parental income exceeds the parental income threshold by any amount up to $3,713.32, the Student Allowance (gross) payable is reduced as follows:

| Parental income minus parental income threshold | = A (parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold) |
| --- | --- |
| Multiply A by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) (at 1 April 2026) | = B (amount the gross Student Allowance rate will be reduced) |
| Student Allowance rate (gross) minus B | = C (Student Allowance rate (gross) payable after abatement, if any) |

## Calculation 2: Annual parental income (gross) exceeds the parental income threshold by more than $3,713.32 (or $71.41 a week)

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $3,713.32 (or $71.41 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payment by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $3,713.32 (or $71.41 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $1,125.24. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate by $1,125.24 and

Step 2: Multiply the remaining amount of parental income that exceeds the parental income threshold (in excess of $3,713.32) by 0.2793296 (i.e. 27.93296%). Further reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by that amount (i.e. after applying the reduction in step 1).

## Example - Calculation 2: A student's parents have annual parental income of $90,507.43 (gross)

|  | Calculation using gross annual figures | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parental income threshold (from 1 April 2026) | $72,108.92 | $1,386.71 |
| Calculate if parental income over the threshold | $90,507.43 - $72,108.92 = $18,398.51 | $1,740.52 - $1,386.71 = $353.81 |
| Calculation | Step 1 : $3,713.32 x 0.3030303 = $1,125.24 | Step 1 : $71.41 x 0.3030303 = $21.63 |
| Step 2 : $18,398.51 - $3,713.32 = $14,685.19 | Step 2 : $353.81 - $71.41 = $282.40 |  |
| $14,685.19 x 0.2793296 = $4,102.00 | $353.81 x 0.2793296 = $98.82 |  |
| Student Allowance (gross) payment (from 1 April 2026) | $16,725.28 Less $1,125.24 (step 1) Less $5,138.64 (step 2) | $321.64 Less $21.63 (step 1) Less $98.82 (step 2) |
| = $10,461.40 annual Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) | = $201.19 weekly Student Allowance (gross) payable (after abatement) |  |

Note Figures are not rounded or truncated during calculation, but the final Student Allowance payable is truncated to 2 decimal places.

When the gross annual parental income is over the parental income threshold by more than $13,494.52 (or $259.51 a week), reduce the gross Student Allowance payable by the total sum of step 1 and 2:

Step 1: Multiply $13,494.52 (or $259.51 a week) by 0.3030303 (i.e. 30.30303%) = $4,089.24. Reduce the annual gross Student Allowance rate payable by $3,455.95 and

|  | Calculation using gross annual figure | Calculation using average gross weekly figures |

A higher rate of Student Allowance is paid if the couple's combined income per week is less than the combined income threshold.

If the couple's combined weekly gross income is more than the combined income threshold but less than combined income cut out point, then Student Allowance will be paid at a lower rate.

In any week that a couple's combined weekly gross income is higher than the combined income cut out point there will be no entitlement to a Student Allowance.

The combined income thresholds and cut out points were not adjusted from 1 April 1998 to 31 December 2005, nor from 1 January 2006 to 31 March 2008. The increase from 1 January 2006 occurred alongside the replacement of the cliff-face threshold with a "dollar for dollar" abatement above the personal income threshold of $180.00.

From 1 April 2008 the threshold and cut out points have been adjusted each year in accordance with the change in CPI.

## Previous parental income abatement calculations

Below are the Student Allowances previous parental income abatement calculations.

## Living at home rate

## Living away from home rate

From 1 April 2022, there are 2 separate abatement calculations depending on the amount the parental income (gross) exceeds the parental income threshold. The 2 abatement calculations used are for students 'Living at home' and 'Living away from home'.

These abatement calculations change each year as part of the annual general adjustment (AGA).

## From 1 January 2005

From 1 January 2005, the tables were replaced with a calculation. Originally, the calculation was a 25 cent deduction from the gross Student Allowance for every $1.00 of parental income over the threshold until the income reached the cut-out point.

As this is a calculation of a gross income to determine a net rate, when the lower income tax thresholds changed, the percentage amount changed accordingly.

The percentages that have been used are:

| Date | Percentage used in calculation |
| --- | --- |
| From 1 October 2008 to 31 March 2011 | 28.57143 |
| From 19 January 2007 to 30 September 2008 | 29.41176 |
| From 1 January 2005 to 18 January 2007 | 25 |

## From 1 January 1999 to 31 December 2004

From 1 January 1999 to 31 December 2004 there was no standard Student Allowance abatement calculation. Instead, the appropriate rate of payment when a parental income test was applied was specified in the Student Allowances Regulations 1998. See:

documents.text:
## Compulsory fees

There is no limit on the amount of compulsory fees that can be borrowed and paid to an Education Provider using a Student Loan. The amount paid will be the amount the Education Provider requests.

The one exception is compulsory fees for pilot training. For study starting on or after 1 January 2013, the maximum amount that may be borrowed is $35,000 per 1 EFTS.

For more information see:

- Borrowing limit - pilot training

There is a limit on the maximum annual increase in compulsory fees that an education provider can set for most courses or qualifications. This is known as the "Annual Maximum Fee Movement" (AMFM). It is administered by the Tertiary Education Commission.

For more information see:

- Tertiary Education Commission Annual Maximum Fee Movement (AMFM)

## Historical information

When the Student Loan scheme was introduced in 1992 there was a fee cap on private training establishments of $4,500.

From 1 January 1997 this was increased to $6,500.

From 1 January 2005 this fee cap was removed.

The maximum living cost component is reduced by any Student Allowance received.

The original weekly limit of $150 was set in 1995 as a result of a review of the Student Loan scheme. That rate took effect from 1 January 1997.
